brief.situation: You are the analyst on the early shift in the security operations center (SOC) at Quillon Freight, a fictional logistics company. At 07:00 four alerts sit in the queue: a critical antivirus detection, a high-severity burst of VPN failures, a medium EDR alert about certutil, and a low IDS port sweep. One of them is a live intrusion. Triage them, contain what is real, preserve evidence and report.
handover: EDR covers every Windows host and can network-isolate one. svc-backup is a service account with administrator rights on the finance servers.
The vulnerability scanner at 192.0.2.10 runs every weekday from 06:00 to 08:00.
howItWorks: Each task takes analyst time: choose it, then let the work finish, which moves the clock by the minutes that task takes. The attacker keeps working on the same clock.
New alerts and log lines appear in the console as they happen.
When you declare the incident contained, you notify, write the record and explain your reasoning.

writeup.question: For the incident record: how you decided which alert was the intrusion, what you contained and why, and what you kept as evidence.

parts.label: Triage
parts.criteria: Ranks by evidence, not the severity label: certutil downloading from an outside address under an encoded PowerShell launched by Word is a living-off-the-land intrusion; a quarantined file with nothing since and a spray with no success were stopped by controls; the sweep is the scheduled scanner (a false positive to tune).
parts.modelAnswer: The medium certutil alert was the real one: Word started an encoded PowerShell, certutil downloaded a file from 203.0.113.45 and rundll32 ran it and beaconed. The critical quarantine and the VPN spray were already stopped, and the sweep was our scanner in its window.

parts.label: Containment and scope
parts.criteria: Isolates the host with EDR at once (blocking the address alone fails because the implant changes address); treats credentials cached on the host as stolen once LSASS was read and disables or resets them; hunts every endpoint for the same pattern.
parts.modelAnswer: I isolated FIN-WS07 through EDR rather than only blocking the address, hunted all endpoints for the certutil and rundll32 pattern, and would disable svc-backup if LSASS had been read.

parts.label: Evidence
parts.criteria: Captures memory and the EDR triage package before reimaging; builds a timeline back to the macro document.
parts.modelAnswer: I took memory and the triage package into the case file before any reimage, and the timeline put initial access at the 06:38 invoice document.

expertPath.text: Read the medium certutil alert before the critical one: an encoded PowerShell and certutil fetching from an outside address is a live intrusion. Call it an incident and isolate FIN-WS07 with EDR.
Escalate; capture memory and the triage package; hunt every endpoint for the pattern; build the timeline back to the macro document.

contained.headline: Good: the right alert, first
contained.body: You judged each alert on its evidence. The critical label was a quarantine that had already worked; the medium one was the intrusion.

containedLate.headline: Contained, with gaps
containedLate.body: The attacker is out. The criteria show what cost you: time on the loud alerts, a later isolation, or a second host.

exfil.headline: Data uploaded out
exfil.body: Blocking one address or working the alerts by severity label left the implant running. Isolate the host, not the indicator.

evidenceLost.headline: Evidence wiped
evidenceLost.body: Reimaging before a memory capture destroys what the implant did and which credentials it read. Collect, then rebuild.

stillIn.headline: Closed too soon
stillIn.body: Once LSASS was read, every credential cached on the host is stolen. Disable or reset them, and isolate every host they reached.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: Severity labels describe the rule, not the incident. The quarantine and the VPN spray were stopped by controls, and the sweep was the scheduled scanner; the medium certutil alert, with Word spawning an encoded PowerShell, certutil downloading and rundll32 beaconing, was the live intrusion. Isolate FIN-WS07 with EDR, escalate, capture memory and the triage package, hunt every endpoint for the pattern, treat credentials cached there as stolen if LSASS was touched, and build the timeline back to the macro document.
